It closed in tight; then, when its links were fastened hardest, * it opened, though I had thought it never would.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. ḍāqa bihi (or lahu) dharʿan, “to be straitened in reach”, to find a thing beyond one's power. ḥalaqāt, “rings, links”, of a chain or a noose. The print points farajat, “it opened”, active, beside the passive tufraju, “be opened”, at the line's end. The print runs lā tufraju together as لَاتُفْرَجُ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا سَكَنَا فِي تِلْكَ الْجَزِيرَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahumā sakanā fī tilka al-jazīrati
sentences.l: Then they-two dwelt in that island.
sentences.i: Then the two of them settled on that island.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا طَيْرُ الْمَاءِ مَسْرُورًا أَمِنًا انْسَاقَ الْقَضَاءُ إِلَيْهِ بَازِيًا جَائِعًا فَضَرَبَهُ بِمِخْلَبِهِ فِي بَطْنِهِ ضَرْبَةً فَقَتَلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā ṭayru al-māʾi masrūran aminan insāqa al-qaḍāʾu ilayhi bāziyan jāʾiʿan fa-ḍarabahu bi-mikhlabihi fī baṭnihi ḍarbatan fa-qatalahu
sentences.l: And while the water-bird (was) happy, safe, the decree was-driven to him (as) a hungry falcon, and it struck-him with its talon in his belly a blow and killed-him.
sentences.i: But one day, while the water-bird was living happy and secure, fate sent him a hungry falcon, which struck him one blow in the belly with its talons and killed him.
sentences.n: baynamā, “while”, followed by a noun and two accusatives, masrūran aminan, as if kāna, “was”, stood before them: the verb is left to be understood. insāqa is Form VII of sāqa, “to drive”, and should mean “was driven”; here it seems to be used as if it were sāqa, “fate drove to him a hungry falcon”, which is how bāziyan, in the accusative, is taken. The likelier sense is clear; the grammar is loose. bāzī, “falcon, hawk”. The hamza in أمنا is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يُغْنِ عَنْهُ الْحَذَرُ عِنْدَ فَرَاغِ الْأَجَلِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yughni ʿanhu al-ḥadharu ʿinda farāghi al-ajali
sentences.l: And the caution did-not avail him, at the running-out of the appointed-term.
sentences.i: Caution was no help to him once his appointed time had run out.
sentences.n: aghnā ʿan, “to avail, be of use to”; lam yughni is its jussive. ajal, “the appointed term”, the hour of death. It is the duck's lesson in the last night over again.

sentences.t: وَسَبَبُ قَتْلِهِ غَفْلَتُهُ عَنِ التَّسْبِيحِ
sentences.tr: wa-sababu qatlihi ghaflatuhu ʿani al-tasbīḥi
sentences.l: And the cause of his killing (was) his neglect of the glorification.
sentences.i: He was killed because he had grown careless of praising God.
sentences.n: ghafla ʿan, “heedlessness of, neglect of”. tasbīḥ, saying subḥāna allāh, “glory be to God”; the peahen gave the same reason for the duck's death.

sentences.t: قِيلَ إِنَّ تَسْبِيحَهُ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا فِيمَا قَدَّرَ وَدَبَّرَ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا فِيمَا أَغْنَى وَأَفْقَرَ
sentences.tr: qīla inna tasbīḥahu subḥāna rabbinā fīmā qaddara wa-dabbara subḥāna rabbinā fīmā aghnā wa-afqara
sentences.l: It was-said that his glorification (was): Glory to our Lord in what He-decreed and arranged! Glory to our Lord in what He-made-rich and made-poor!
sentences.i: His praise, it is said, was: Glory be to our Lord in all He decrees and ordains! Glory be to our Lord in all that He gives and takes away!
sentences.n: qaddara, “to decree, measure out”; dabbara, “to order, arrange”: the pair rhymes, as do aghnā and afqara, “He made rich” and “He made poor”. The shaddas in قدّر and دبّر are the print's own.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ حَدِيثِ طَيْرِ الْمَاءِ وَجَوَارِحِ الطُّيُورِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min ḥadīthi ṭayri al-māʾi wa-jawāriḥi al-ṭuyūri
sentences.l: This (is) what was of the story of the water-bird and the hunting-ones of the birds.
sentences.i: That is the story of the water-bird and the birds of prey.
sentences.n: jawāriḥ (sing. jāriḥa), “beasts and birds of prey”, from jaraḥa, “to wound”, also “to hunt, catch”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ يَا شَهْرَزَادُ لَقَدْ زِدْتِنِي بِحِكَايَتِكِ مَوَاعِظَ وَاعْتِبَارًا فَهَلْ عِنْدَكِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ حِكَايَاتِ الْوُحُوشِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku yā Shahrazādu la-qad zidtinī bi-ḥikāyatiki mawāʿiẓa wa-iʿtibāran fa-hal ʿindaki shayʾun min ḥikāyāti al-wuḥūshi
sentences.l: And the king said: O Shahrazād, you have indeed increased-me by your tale (in) admonitions and taking-of-lessons; so is-there with you anything of the tales of the wild-beasts?
sentences.i: The king said, “Shahrazād, your tale has given me more to take to heart and more to learn from. Do you know any stories of the wild beasts?”
sentences.n: zāda, “to increase”, takes two objects: zidtinī … mawāʿiẓa, “you have increased me in admonitions”. mawāʿiẓ (sing. mawʿiẓa), “admonitions, lessons”. wuḥūsh (sing. waḥsh), “wild animals”, as against the birds of the tales before.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ نَعَمْ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ ثَعْلَبًا وَذِئْبًا أَلِفَا وَكْرًا فَكَانَا يَأْوِيَانِ إِلَيْهِ مَعَ بَعْضِهِمَا وَيَبِيتَانِ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: qālat naʿam iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna thaʿlaban wa-dhiʾban alifā wakran fa-kānā yaʾwiyāni ilayhi maʿa baʿḍihimā wa-yabītāni fīhi
sentences.l: She said: Yes. Know, O king, that a fox and a wolf grew-accustomed-to a lair, and they-two used-to take-shelter in-it with each-other and spend-the-night in-it.
sentences.i: She said: Yes. Know, O king, that a fox and a wolf shared a den they had grown used to, where they took shelter together and spent their nights.
sentences.n: A new tale begins, of the wolf and the fox. alifa, “to become familiar with, grow used to”. wakr is properly a bird's nest, here a lair. The hamza and sukūn in يأْويان and the tanwīn on وكرًا are the print's own.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الذِّئْبُ قَاهِرًا لِلثَّعْلَبِ فَلَبِثَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ مُدَّةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-dhiʾbu qāhiran li-al-thaʿlabi fa-labithā ʿalā dhālika muddatan mina al-zamāni
sentences.l: And the wolf was overpowering to the fox; and they-two remained on that (footing) a span of the time.
sentences.i: The wolf used to bully the fox, and so they went on for some time.
sentences.n: qāhir, “subduing, overpowering”: the wolf lorded it over the fox. labitha ʿalā dhālika, “to stay in that state”. The shadda in مدّة is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّ الثَّعْلَبَ أَشَارَ عَلَى الذِّئْبِ بِالرِّفْقِ وَتَرْكِ الْفَسَادِ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa anna al-thaʿlaba ashāra ʿalā al-dhiʾbi bi-al-rifqi wa-tarki al-fasādi
sentences.l: And it chanced that the fox advised the wolf to gentleness and the leaving-off of the mischief.
sentences.i: Then one day the fox advised the wolf to be gentle and give up his wicked ways,
sentences.n: ittafaqa anna, “it happened that”. ashāra ʿalā … bi-, “to advise someone to (do something)”. rifq, “gentleness, kindness”; fasād, “corruption, mischief”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ إِنْ دُمْتَ عَلَى عُتُوِّكَ رُبَّمَا سَلَّطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ ابْنَ آدَمَ فَإِنَّهُ ذُوحِيَلٍ وَمَكْرٍ وَخِدَاعٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu iʿlam in dumta ʿalā ʿutuwwika rubbamā sallaṭa allāhu ʿalayka ibna Ādama fa-innahu dhū ḥiyalin wa-makrin wa-khidāʿin
sentences.l: And he said to him: Know: if you-persist in your insolence, perhaps God will-set-over you the Son of Adam; for he (is) possessor-of tricks and cunning and deceit.
sentences.i: saying, “Know that if you keep up your insolence, God may well set the Son of Adam upon you; for he is full of tricks and cunning and deceit.
sentences.n: ان after iʿlam would usually be anna, “that”; here it is read in, “if”, since a conditional follows: dumta, “you persist”. rubbamā, “perhaps”, opens the answer without fa-. ʿutuww, “insolence, arrogance”. sallaṭa ʿalā, “to give (someone) power over”. The print runs dhū ḥiyalin together as ذوحيل; the spacing is kept. The shadda in عتوّك is the print's own.

sentences.t: يَصِيدُ الطَّيْرَ مِنَ الْجَوِّ وَالْحُوتَ مِنَ الْبَحْرِ وَيَقْطَعُ الْجِبَالَ وَيَنْقُلُهَا مِنْ مَكَانٍ إِلَى مَكَانٍ وَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ حِيَلِهِ وَمَكْرِهِ
sentences.tr: yaṣīdu al-ṭayra mina al-jawwi wa-al-ḥūta mina al-baḥri wa-yaqṭaʿu al-jibāla wa-yanquluhā min makānin ilā makānin wa-kullu dhālika min ḥiyalihi wa-makrihi
sentences.l: He-hunts the birds from the air and the fish from the sea, and he-cuts the mountains and moves-them from place to place; and all of that (is) from his tricks and his cunning.
sentences.i: He catches the birds out of the air and the fish out of the sea; he hews the mountains and carries them from place to place; and all of it by his tricks and his cunning.
sentences.n: ḥūt, “fish”, often a large one. qaṭaʿa al-jibāla, “to cut the mountains”: to quarry stone from them. The shadda in الجوّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَعَلَيْكَ بِالرِّفْقِ وَالْإِنْصَافِ وَتَرْكِ الشَّرِّ وَالِاعْتِسَافِ فَإِنَّهُ أَهْنَى لِعَيْشِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿalayka bi-al-rifqi wa-al-inṣāfi wa-tarki al-sharri wa-al-iʿtisāfi fa-innahu ahnā li-ʿayshika
sentences.l: So upon-you (be) the gentleness and the fairness, and the leaving-off of the evil and the oppression; for it (is) more-pleasant for your living.
sentences.i: So hold to gentleness and fair dealing, and give up wickedness and tyranny; your life will be the sweeter for it.”
sentences.n: ʿalayka bi-, “hold to, keep to”, a set phrase of urging. inṣāf, “fair dealing”; iʿtisāf, “injustice, high-handedness”: the two rhyme. ahnā, “more pleasant”, is ahnaʾ with the hamza softened.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَقْبَلِ الذِّئْبُ قَوْلَهُ وَأَغْلَظَ لَهُ الرَّدَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yaqbali al-dhiʾbu qawlahu wa-aghlaẓa lahu al-radda
sentences.l: And the wolf did-not accept his saying, and made-harsh to him the reply.
sentences.i: The wolf would not listen, and answered him roughly.
sentences.n: aghlaẓa lahu al-radda, “he was rough with him in reply”. The shadda in الردّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ مَالَكَ وَالْكَلَامَ فِي عَظِيمِ الْأُمُورِ وَجَسِيمِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu mā laka wa-al-kalāma fī ʿaẓīmi al-umūri wa-jasīmihā
sentences.l: And he said to him: What (is) to-you and the talking about the great of the matters and the weighty-of-them?
sentences.i: He said, “What business have you talking about great and weighty matters?”
sentences.n: mā laka wa-…, “what have you to do with …?”: after this wa- the noun goes into the accusative. The print runs mā laka together as مالك; the spacing is kept. ʿaẓīm and jasīm, “great” and “weighty”, a near-synonym pair.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ لَطَمَ الثَّعْلَبَ لَطْمَةً فَخَرَّ مِنْهَا مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma laṭama al-thaʿlaba laṭmatan fa-kharra minhā maghshiyyan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then he struck the fox a slap, and he fell from-it fainted-upon.
sentences.i: Then he struck the fox such a blow that he fell down senseless.
sentences.n: laṭama, “to slap, strike with the flat of the hand”, here with a paw. maghshiyyan ʿalayhi, “in a faint”, literally “one overcome upon”. The shadda in فخرّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ ضَحِكَ فِي وَجْهِ الذِّئْبِ وَأَقْبَلَ مُعْتَذِرًا إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ الشَّيْنِ قَائِلًا لَهُ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqa ḍaḥika fī wajhi al-dhiʾbi wa-aqbala muʿtadhiran ilayhi mina al-kalāmi al-shayni qāʾilan lahu hādhayni al-baytayni shiʿrun
sentences.l: And when he came-to, he laughed in the face of the wolf, and came-forward apologising to him for the shameful speech, saying to him these two verses — verse:
sentences.i: When he came round, he smiled in the wolf's face and came forward to beg his pardon for his unseemly words, reciting to him these two lines:
sentences.n: ḍaḥika fī wajhihi, “he laughed in his face”: here a smile of appeasement, not mockery. iʿtadhara ilā … min, “to apologise to someone for”. shayn, “disgrace, something shameful”, a noun used as an adjective: “speech that brings shame”. shiʿr, “verse”, is the rubric that introduces the lines.

sentences.t:
اِنْ كُنْتُ قَدْ اَذْنَبْتُ ذَنْبًا سَالِفاً * فِيْ حُبِّكُمْ وَأَتَيْتُ شَيْأً مُنْكَراً
اَنَا تَائِبٌ عَمَّا جَنَيْتُ وَعَفْوُكُمْ * يَسَعُ الْمُسِيءَ اِذَا اَتَى مُسْتَغْفِراً
sentences.tr:
in kuntu qad adhnabtu dhanban sālifan * fī ḥubbikum wa-ataytu shayʾan munkaran
anā tāʾibun ʿammā janaytu wa-ʿafwukum * yasaʿu al-musīʾa idhā atā mustaghfiran
sentences.l:
If I have sinned a sin past * in (my) love-for-you, and brought a thing disapproved,
I (am) repentant of what I-committed, and your pardon * has-room-for the wrongdoer when he-comes asking-forgiveness.
sentences.i:
If in the past I have sinned against you * out of my love, and done a thing amiss,
I repent of the wrong I did; and your pardon * has room for the sinner who comes asking forgiveness.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's own. Lines from the language of love, turned to an apology. -kum, “you” plural, is the respectful plural used to one person. munkar, “disapproved, wrong”. wasiʿa, “to have room for, embrace”.

sentences.t: فَقَبِلَ الذِّئْبُ عُذْرَهُ وَكَفَّ عَنْهُ أَشْرَارَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qabila al-dhiʾbu ʿudhrahu wa-kaffa ʿanhu ashrārahu
sentences.l: And the wolf accepted his excuse and held-back from him his evils,
sentences.i: The wolf accepted his apology and held back his malice from him,
sentences.n: ashrār is properly the plural of sharīr, “wicked men”; here it plainly means the wolf's ill-doing, as if it were a plural of sharr, “evil”. The shadda in كفّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ لَا تَتَكَلَّمْ فِيمَا لَا يَعْنِيكَ تَسْمَعْ مَالَا يُرْضِيكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu lā tatakallam fīmā lā yaʿnīka tasmaʿ mā lā yurḍīka
sentences.l: And he said to him: Do-not speak about what does-not concern-you, (or) you-will-hear what does-not please-you.
sentences.i: and said, “Do not meddle in what is no concern of yours, or you will hear what you will not like.”
sentences.n: A proverb, usually “whoever talks of what does not concern him hears what does not please him”. tasmaʿ, jussive, answers the prohibition, and the sense is “or else you will hear”: a loose but common way of putting it. yaʿnīka and yurḍīka rhyme. The print runs mā lā together as مالا; the spacing is kept.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she ceased the speech allowed her.
